owner_instructions.what_changed: Two independent locks in src/sec10k/web/app.py. (1) ARMING: a credential ALONE never arms paid work — the server refuses to escalate unless SEC10K_ESCALATION_ENABLED=1 is also set; deliberately a second variable, not a truthiness check on the key. (2) PROCESS-WIDE BUDGET: one llm.Budget for the life of the server process (SEC10K_ESCALATION_MAX_CALLS default 20, SEC10K_ESCALATION_MAX_USD default $5.00), passed to every extract_items call, so the ceiling bounds the DEPLOYMENT and not each document. Not silent: /api/meta publishes escalation_enabled, the page disables the checkbox and says why, and a request that asked anyway comes back with an escalation_disarmed message. llm.Budget's docstring no longer claims 'per-run' — it states exactly what one instance bounds and who must pass one to get a per-sweep ceiling.
owner_instructions.verified: With a key exported and the arming var unset: escalation_enabled=false, no routing record, cost all zeros, escalation_disarmed message present. Armed with a 1-call ceiling: request 1 attempts a tier, requests 2 and 3 return outcome=unavailable / 'budget spent: 1 of 1 calls used' — the ceiling is shared across requests, not reset per document. Local runs are unaffected: the eval suites, escalate._demo and a direct extract_items call all bypass web.app.
owner_instructions.not_fixed: The deployment still has no authentication and no rate limit, so an anonymous caller can consume the process budget and deny the capability to others. Spend is bounded; availability is not. Stated in ADR-036 §h2's closing paragraph and carried as a new debt row rather than left implicit.

findings.fix: (a) escalate.verify rejects any proposed code whose item status is not in SPAN_STATUSES ('extracted', 'incorporated_by_reference'), with the reason naming the coverage consequence; (b) envelope_shape now asserts the contract's null-span rule in BOTH directions — a missing/omitted item may not carry offsets and a span-carrying status may not have null ones — so the guard binds every producer, not just the one that broke it, and specs/001-sec10k-contract.md records that the rule is enforced from 2026-08-27; (c) evals/adversarial/escalation-verify-guards.json covers it, watched red at 88b4488.
findings.red_first: Reviewer's repro reproduced exactly: verify accepted a proposal for a `missing` item with rejections=[], apply wrote start=52 end=4064 method=llm_localize with status still 'missing', and meta.coverage moved 0.0030 -> 0.6142 on one item. Full output in pr58-r1-red.txt.

The sharp demonstration, where similarity passes and only the status guard rejects, is escalate._demo's R1 block, which R3 wires into CI in this same commit. Both the case's provenance and the red record say this in full rather than presenting the fixture-level red as stronger than it is.

findings.chose: made the code match the claim, not the claim match the code
findings.fix: verify now returns ({}, why) whenever any NON-NULL proposed span failed any check. A null answer is explicitly not a failure — 'I could not locate item 8' is the honest answer the prompt asks for and must not discard a valid sibling. ADR-036 §b carries a marked correction saying the paragraph was FALSE as first published and why the claim was kept: the ordering check is a property of the item list as a whole.
findings.red_first: A mixed proposal that does NOT trip INV-S1 as a side effect — item 8's real body plus a 40-char stub for item 1 — was partially applied: accepted ['8'] with the sibling rejected. That side-effect trap is exactly why _demo had never watched this property, and the new _demo block and eval case both avoid it.
